title: The Federal Reserve separates financial-system resilience from household credit pressure and inflation risk
source_unit: Federal Reserve Board Financial Stability Report and Monetary Policy Report; US financial-system, macroeconomic, and policy aggregates

observations.period: May 2026 Financial Stability Report; conditions/data through April 23, 2026

asset_valuation_vulnerability.unit: Federal Reserve assessment across equity, corporate debt, residential real estate, and Treasury term premiums

business_household_debt_vulnerability.unit: Federal Reserve assessment; debt-to-GDP continued to trend down

household_credit_stress.value: credit-card and auto-loan delinquencies remained above levels prevailing over the prior decade; mortgage delinquencies remained low overall with distress in selected FHA/VA and low-down-payment groups

financial_sector_leverage.value: notable; hedge-fund leverage near all-time highs and concentrated among large funds

runnable_money_like_liabilities.unit: billions of US dollars at end-2025; 12.0% growth from 2024 Q4 to 2025 Q4

salient_risk_categories.value: geopolitical risks, oil shock, AI, private credit, and persistent inflation

observations.method: Federal Reserve Board monitoring framework organized around asset valuations, borrowing, financial-sector leverage, funding risks, and near-term shocks; report is an institutional assessment rather than a single estimator.
observations.uncertainty: The report identifies vulnerabilities and plausible shocks, not probabilities or realized losses. Aggregate debt, delinquency, leverage, and funding measures have different units and populations; market-contact risk responses are not a representative public-opinion sample.
observations.subgroup: Households, businesses, banks, hedge funds, insurers, money-market funds, private-credit vehicles, and financial markets; selected FHA/VA and low-down-payment borrowers are explicitly distinct household-risk subgroups.
observations.counterinterpretation: A resilient banking sector can coexist with credit stress among particular households or firms. Moderate aggregate debt vulnerability does not mean equal access to credit, and elevated valuations do not establish an imminent correction.

observations.period: July 2026 Monetary Policy Report; data through May 2026 and 2026 Q1/June labor data where specified

denominator.unit: Federal Reserve Board monetary-policy report to Congress

household_consumption_growth.unit: percent average annualized rate through first five months of 2026

federal_funds_target_range.unit: percent since beginning of 2026, as reported July 2026

credit_access.value: broadly available to most nonfinancial firms, households, and municipalities, but relatively tight for small businesses and households

ai_investment_context.value: high-tech investment and data-center-related demand supported activity; AI-related investment partly offset foreign headwinds

observations.method: Federal Reserve Monetary Policy Report submitted to Congress under Section 2B; policy and economic assessment based on information available through the report's stated dates.
observations.uncertainty: The report mixes high-frequency market data, national accounts, labor indicators, and policy judgments with different reference dates. Inflation and consumption measures are aggregates and do not establish household-specific affordability or welfare; the policy rate is not a borrower-specific interest rate.
observations.subgroup: Households, small businesses, nonfinancial firms, workers, financial institutions, and sectors tied to high-tech/data-center investment; demographic employment disparities are discussed separately.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable unemployment and solid productivity can coexist with elevated inflation, tight credit for selected borrowers, weak housing activity, or uneven real-wage gains. Strong AI investment does not establish broad household productivity or worker control.

related_sources.claim: Fed funding-risk section supplies runnable-liability amounts, redemption, and liquidity-transformation context.
Fed Summary of Economic Projections supplies the policy committee projection framework and information date.
IMF Article IV supplies a separate country-surveillance and fiscal/external-risk frame.

boundary: This record separates Federal Reserve financial-stability monitoring from monetary-policy reporting. It contributes institutional risk, credit-access, inflation, labor, consumption, and policy-setting context, but does not establish household welfare, firm incidence, worker power, cultural meaning, political response, or geopolitical leverage.
